geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

peak.note: 17 stacks up at Los Gatos from mid-afternoon
weekend beach traffic northbound in the evening
101 south through Sunnyvale is stop-and-go from 4
101 north is the worst of the peninsula — 280 is usually faster
101 north clogs from Redwood City at 3:30; the 280 split at Daly City is the second squeeze
weekend midday backs up into the city
the Caldecott is the pinch — eastbound clears by 7
Waldo Grade northbound is the bottleneck
Dumbarton eastbound is fine; the toll and the queue are on the way home
local arterials get slow around the school and commute peak

events.title: Social Distortion, Descendents & The Chats
events.note: Three generations of the same impulse on one bill: Mike Ness's tattooed Bakersfield-punk, the Descendents' hyper-caffeinated melody, and Australia's Chats doing pub-rock as farce. They play the Fox tomorrow, so the room is the variable, not the set.

events.title: Aldous Harding
events.note: Sold out. The New Zealand songwriter's voice shifts register between songs like a character actor changing coats, and the theatricality lands better in a 1,400-seat picture palace than in a club. Sam Burton opens with high-lonesome ballads.

events.title: LUCKI
events.note: Chicago rapper whose lo-fi, narcotised delivery made him a reference point for a whole strain of internet rap. Sk8star opens.

events.title: Tokyo Tea Room
events.note: Sold out. English shoegaze-adjacent five-piece with more jangle than fuzz; Beach Vacation opens. A supper-club room with a curtain, which suits the reverb.

events.title: Stephan Jenkins (solo acoustic)
events.note: Sold out. Third Eye Blind's frontman playing a 350-cap room he long outgrew, unplugged. The club closes at the end of the year, which is the reason this one sold out in an afternoon.

events.title: Phora
events.note: Anaheim rapper who built a following on confessional, melodic writing about anxiety and family. The venue's listing showed a $0.00 price, which is more likely a data error than a free show — check before you go.

events.title: Memorizing Alison
events.note: Screening in the Coffee & Language series for the film's 25th anniversary. The Roxie's programming is the reason to read its calendar rather than its marquee.

events.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
events.note: Jane Schoenbrun in person. After We're All Going to the World's Fair and I Saw the TV Glow, a slasher from this director is the most interesting genre proposition of the month.

events.title: Motown on Mondays
events.note: Free before 8, $5 after, and running most Mondays for well over a decade. Straight 45s soul to a room that actually dances on a work night.

events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated
events.note: Projection work thrown up the side of a 1908 skyscraper on Market. Free, outdoors, and better from the far pavement than from underneath it.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden free admission hour
events.note: Free before 10am on Monday, Wednesday and Friday; $12–16 otherwise. An hour in the oldest public Japanese garden in the country for nothing, if you can make an early start.

events.title: Ha Chong-Hyun: Retrospective
events.note: The Dansaekhwa painter who pushed pigment through the back of hemp canvas rather than onto the front of it. Free for all on the first Sunday of the month, which this week means 4 October.

events.title: Fred Wesley's New JBs with Martha High's Funky Divas
events.note: Wesley wrote the horn charts that define the word funk, and Martha High sang behind James Brown for eighteen years. This is the source material, played by the people who cut it.

events.title: Bobby McFerrin & Motion
events.note: A daytime slot — ticketing lists doors at 11:30 for a noon start, which is unusual enough to confirm before you travel. McFerrin's Motion project is improvised vocal music with no net; he also played the Freight last Monday, so this is a residency rather than a repeat listing.

events.title: Art Lande, Günter Wehinger, Tim Wendel
events.note: Free-ish piano trio music in a piano showroom, which is the best-sounding accident in Oakland. Lande has been making quietly strange records since the seventies.

events.title: Devin Gray
events.note: Brooklyn drummer-composer in a tiny Berkeley room. The kind of booking that exists only because someone runs a house series for love.

events.title: cupcakKe
events.note: Chicago rapper whose filthiest bars and her most tender ones sit on the same record, usually the same song. A 1,400-cap ballroom is the right scale now.

events.title: Chanel Beads
events.note: Sold out. Shane Lavers builds songs out of blown-out string samples and half-buried vocals — pop shapes heard through a wall. Horse Vision and urika's bedroom open.

events.title: Brian Fallon & The Painkillers
events.note: The Gaslight Anthem's singer doing the Springsteen-by-way-of-hardcore thing in a 400-cap room, with Tim Barry — ex-Avail, now solo and rawer — opening. All ages.

events.title: Ethan Regan
events.note: With harf. The venue lists no times or prices on its calendar, so treat the 8pm as the house default rather than confirmed.

events.title: The Quiet Men, Greg Hoy & the Boys, Fast & Vengefully
events.note: A local three-band bill at fifteen dollars, which is the club doing the job it exists for. Greg Hoy has been making scrappy power-pop records in this city for twenty years.

events.title: KAL-EL
events.note: Norwegian stoner-metal with Goya supporting. The venue's own monthly calendar pages were returning 503s all day, so this is sourced from the ticketing feed rather than the venue.

events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots
events.note: Thea Musgrave's 1977 opera, back at the house that gave it its American premiere. Musgrave is 98 and wrote the libretto herself; the score's Scottish court is all brass and menace. Two performances left, this and Sunday's matinee.

events.title: Filipiñana
events.note: Part of FiliKula. Rafael Manuel's short feature watches a golf-course tee-girl in Manila with a still, class-conscious eye.

events.title: Gandahar (4K restoration)
events.note: René Laloux's 1988 animated science fiction, the last of the three features he made and the least seen. Rarely projected at all, let alone restored.

events.title: American Doctor
events.note: Co-presented by the Arab Film & Media Institute and the Jewish Film Institute — a pairing that is itself the statement. Also screens Wednesday at 6.

events.title: Ghost in the Shell: 30th Anniversary Remaster
events.note: Oshii's 1995 film in a new transfer. The rain-slicked Hong Kong sequence is the argument for seeing it projected rather than streamed.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: Free lunchtime music and food trucks on the plaza between the library and City Hall. Runs Tuesdays and Thursdays; the bands are local and the point is the hour outdoors.

events.title: Noe Valley Night Market
events.note: Small, weekly, free, and genuinely a neighbourhood thing rather than a pop-up circuit. Makers and food on the square at 24th.

events.title: Ice Cream Social with the Nova Jazz Band
events.note: Trad jazz and free ice cream on a downtown plaza at half past three on a Tuesday. Downtown SF's programming is aimed squarely at office workers and is none the worse for it.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: Emma Rice's stage adaptation opens A.C.T.'s season and runs to 18 October. Rice's work is built out of visible stagecraft, which is a good match for a film about a man pretending to be someone who does not exist.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: The Mischief company's disaster-panto, running to late November. The Playhouse's calendar does not publish per-date curtain times, so the 7pm is the house weekday default.

events.title: Lava Thomas: Lineage
events.note: Thomas works in tambourines, graphite and marble to make monuments to Black women the city never built. Free, and a commercial gallery you should walk into anyway.

events.title: Social Distortion, Descendents & The Chats
events.note: Doors 6. The second of two Bay nights — if you have the choice, the Fox is the better-sounding room and BART drops you at the door.

events.title: Spyro Gyra
events.note: Fifty years of jazz-fusion by a band that has outlasted every genre label applied to it. Two nights. Smooth in the technical sense, not the pejorative one.

events.title: LAUNDRY DAY
events.note: Doors 7. Five New Yorkers who started as teenagers making bedroom pop and have thickened into something closer to a band. A beer hall on Shattuck with a real stage at the back.

events.title: Thelma and the Sleaze
events.note: Nashville's loudest, filthiest boogie band in a 150-cap Albany bar. Lauren Gilbert plays Southern rock like it owes her money.

events.title: Joey Alexander
events.note: The Indonesian pianist who was Grammy-nominated at eleven and is now a serious adult improviser, in a showroom seating maybe eighty. Thirty-five dollars is a mistake in your favour.

events.title: The Cook
events.note: Postshow discussion tonight. Eduardo Machado's play about a cook's forty-year vow to keep a Havana mansion ready for owners who are never coming back. Runs to 11 October.

events.title: Last Tuesdays Comedy
events.note: Free with RSVP, monthly, and the Layover is the rare downtown Oakland bar that feels like a living room. Booked locally rather than by a chain.

events.title: Drive-In Movie Night
events.note: Six dollars a head at one of the last operating drive-ins in the region. Concord is a haul from anywhere, and the price and the novelty are the argument.

events.title: Candlebox with Sponge
events.note: Doors 7. Two 1993 alt-rock survivors on a double bill; Candlebox has been running a long farewell. The Guild carries almost all of the Peninsula's touring music on its own.

events.title: Jon Q Public
events.note: With Three Reefs Deep and ratbastard. Pacifica is not in the region lists — filed Peninsula by proximity. A dive bar behind the fog line, which is most of Pacifica's appeal.

events.title: Matthew West
events.note: Contemporary Christian songwriter with a long radio run, playing a church rather than a shed. Listed for completeness; the audience knows who he is.

events.title: Sips & Sounds of Summer
events.note: Free outdoor music on the park lawn, Tuesdays through August and September — which makes tonight the season's last date. The series' own page does not publish a closing date, so confirm before driving over.

events.title: Beth Orton
events.note: With her band, and Kenny Stahl opening. Orton invented a particular kind of English folk sung over programmed rhythm and has spent the last decade making it stranger rather than smoother. The GAMH balcony is the seat.

events.title: Failure
events.note: The Los Angeles trio whose 1996 Fantastic Planet was ignored on release and has been quietly canonical ever since. quannnic opens. The top ticket tier runs to $235, which is a VIP package rather than the price of entry.

events.title: Chat Pile
events.note: Oklahoma City noise-rock about grim American specifics — rent, meth, a Denny's parking lot. Soul Glo and Virga open, which makes this the heaviest and best-sequenced bill of the week.

events.title: JPEGMAFIA
events.note: Peggy produces, raps and mixes his own chaos; the live show is closer to a hardcore set than a rap one. redveil and matt proxy open.

events.title: Show Me the Body
events.note: Banjo-driven New York hardcore, which sounds like a joke until you hear it. Whispers and Jivebomb open. Expect the floor to be the venue.

events.title: tobi lou
events.note: 21+. Chicago-via-Nigeria rapper with a cartoon-bright palette and a real ear for melody. 3 Feet No Pressure opens.

events.title: Emei
events.note: Sold out. Chinese-American songwriter who came up through a televised singing contest in Shanghai and now writes sharp, funny pop about exactly that. Madelline opens.

events.title: Twin Temple: Satanic Panic, a Drag Ritual
events.note: Peaches Christ presents. Twin Temple play doo-wop and sixties girl-group soul with Satanic lyrics and a live ritual; pairing them with a Peaches Christ production in that theatre is the most San Francisco booking of the week.

events.title: Porch Light
events.note: All ages, with Common People. Local-circuit indie at a price that lets you take a chance on it.

events.title: Cult Strange, Vague Lanes, The Ink Bats
events.note: Three bands, fifteen dollars advance. Post-punk in the specific Bay sense — cheap, loud, local, and gone by eleven.

events.title: DOOM GONG
events.note: With James Wavey. Bass-heavy club music in a room small enough that the low end is a physical fact.

events.title: Author & Punisher
events.note: Tristan Shone plays industrial doom on machines he built himself out of hydraulics and steel. Guiltless and Ex Everything open. The engineering is the point and it is genuinely heavy.

events.title: Cactus Lee
events.note: Austin songwriter working a wry, ramshackle country seam. The venue's own events page could not be read this week, so time and price are unconfirmed.

events.title: Jon Q Public
events.note: With Durango Dogs and Redakted. The Utah has been putting local bands upstairs of a saloon since the 1970s and remains the cheapest way to see four of them.

events.title: Rip Florence
events.note: Mission dive with a back room. Sourced from the ticketing sweep rather than the venue, so treat the time as approximate.

events.title: Nino Msk
events.note: Small Mission room, listing sourced from a ticketing feed that did not carry a time or price. Unverified beyond the date.

events.title: D.E.B.S.
events.note: Sapphic Cinema Social Club. Angela Robinson's 2004 spy spoof, which was a flop and is now a text. The audience is half the screening.

events.title: Barbara Forever
events.note: Director Brydie O'Connor in person for a Q&A. Documentary portrait, short engagement.

events.title: Mysterious Skin (4K restoration)
events.note: Co-presented by Frameline. Araki's 2004 film is his most controlled and his hardest to sit through; the restoration is reason enough to face it again.

events.title: Free admission day at YBCA
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Galleries free every Wednesday, which is the point of the institution. Three shows are up: Dread Scott's The Body Politic, Rael San Fratello's Prototypes and Provocations, and GaHee Park's paintings.

events.title: Free art workshop: 3D paper flowers
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Free with registration, in the Grand Lobby. Paired with a 4pm gallery tour and sketching session in the GaHee Park show.

events.title: Free bandshell concert: three live bands
events.note: Three hours of free music at the Golden Gate Park bandshell on a Wednesday afternoon, two days before the park fills up for the festival. The Golden Gate Park Band's own 144th season closed on 27 September, so this is separate programming.

events.title: Critic to Critic: food criticism and Bay Area restaurants
events.note: MacKenzie Chung Fegan and Michael Bauer, two Chronicle critics a generation apart, on what the job is now. Presented with the Chronicle in the Grand Theater.

events.title: Madrone Artist Grant Showcase
events.note: Free. The bar gives small grants to local artists and then hangs the results. Low-stakes, actual art, no admission.

events.title: German Game Night
events.note: Monthly, free, board games in German. Filed under worthwhile oddities without hesitation.

events.title: The Big Quiz Thing Live
events.note: Free. A quiz with production values, which is rarer than it sounds.

events.title: Astronomy on Tap SF
events.note: Free with a one-drink minimum. Working astronomers give short talks in a bar; the questions afterwards are the good part.

events.title: Weekly swing dance night with live music
events.note: Fifteen dollars, live band, beginner lesson first. The Bay's swing scene runs on nights like this rather than on festivals.

events.title: Rooftop stargazing night
events.note: Free public telescope time on top of a university building. Fog west of Twin Peaks decides whether you see anything, so check the sky before you commit.

events.title: East Meets West: Japanese metal and cosplay party
events.note: Free, RSVP encouraged, runs to 2am. A Mission dive given over to Japanese metal and visual-kei for a night.

events.title: AURA
events.note: Light and sound installation under the nave, two sittings at 7:15 and 8:30. The building does most of the work and that is not a criticism.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: A.C.T.'s season opener, mid-run. See Tuesday's note.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Curtain time is the house default rather than a published one.

events.title: Walking tour: Downtown Deco
events.note: Two hours of 1920s and 30s facades starting at the Pacific Telephone building, which is the best of them. Downtown SF runs these midweek and midafternoon.

events.title: Jack Johnson with G. Love
events.note: First of two nights. The Greek outdoors in early October is the best room in the region and will be cold by nine — bring a layer. BART to Downtown Berkeley and walk up.

events.title: Spyro Gyra
events.note: Second night. See Tuesday.

events.title: Cardinals
events.note: Doors 7. Irish five-piece making unhurried, Van-Morrison-shaped guitar music; one of the more convincing recent exports from Dublin.

events.title: buddy junior, Quinine, IX of Swords
events.note: A 150-cap room on Telegraph and three local bands. The club's own calendar renders client-side and fetches empty, so this comes off the JamBase mirror.

events.title: Self-Portrait Along the Borderline
events.note: Anna Dziapshipa's essay film about a Georgian-Abkhaz family house and what a border does to a family. Part of BAMPFA's Caucasus programming.

events.title: The Cook
events.note: Mid-run. See Tuesday.

events.title: Pat Benatar & Neil Giraldo
events.note: Forty-odd years of the same marriage and the same guitar tone, outdoors on a hillside above Saratoga. The shuttle from the lower lot is not optional.

events.title: Brujeria
events.note: With Ethnocide, Mortal and Sodomy. The Spanish-language death-metal collective that has been a running joke and a genuinely brutal band for thirty-five years.

events.title: Roosters Comedy Showcase
events.note: Standing weekly showcase at the South Bay's long-running comedy club. Listed for completeness; the information value is low unless you already go.

events.title: Spirit + Sound
events.note: A hotel-bar sound series on the Peninsula, found only in the ticketing sweep. Nothing about the billing was verifiable — descriptor is lower-confidence.

events.title: An Evening Honoring Steve Earle
events.note: Emmylou Harris, Jackson Browne, Gillian Welch & David Rawlings, Buddy Miller, Elizabeth Cook and Hot Tuna, all on one stage for Earle, with proceeds to Sweetwater Spectrum. This is the ticketed kickoff to Hardly Strictly and the single best-assembled bill of the week — most of these people then play the park for free.

events.title: Renée Fleming Sings Strauss
events.note: A matinee, which is unusual for an opening subscription week. Fleming in the Four Last Songs with Santtu-Matias Rouvali making his SF Symphony debut — a soprano who has sung this music for thirty years and a conductor who has not. Repeats Saturday evening and Sunday afternoon.

events.title: Los Thuthanaka
events.note: Elysia Crampton and Chuquimamani-Condori, siblings working from Aymara music into something abrasive and devotional at once. Nothing else this week sounds remotely like it.

events.title: Soda Blonde
events.note: Dublin four-piece out of the ashes of Little Green Cars, writing big-chorused, slightly bruised pop. Marika Christine opens.

events.title: of Montreal
events.note: Sold out. Kevin Barnes's psychedelic vaudeville in a 350-cap room, which is a fraction of where this band usually plays. Healing Potpourri open. One of the hardest tickets of the week.

events.title: Michelle Branch with SASAMI
events.note: Sold out, first of two added nights. SASAMI is the reason to care about the bill — her last record was a lurching, metal-adjacent turn that has nothing to do with early-2000s radio pop.

events.title: Saint Harison
events.note: Sold out, all ages. Canadian singer working a falsetto-heavy, church-inflected R&B seam.

events.title: Mari Froes
events.note: Sold out. Brazilian pop songwriter whose audience arrived via the internet rather than radio, which is why a 500-cap room went first.

events.title: Miss Hits / Litty Debungus
events.note: All ages, with I Am the Octopus. A cheap local bill with better band names than most.

events.title: POiSON GiRL FRiEND
events.note: Noriko Sekiguchi's early-nineties Japanese dream-pop project, revived and touring for the first time. A cult record finally getting a room.

events.title: Don West
events.note: With KESMAR. August Hall publishes no times or prices; 8pm is the house default.

events.title: Carbon Leaf
events.note: Virginia Celtic-inflected roots band, twenty-five years in and still touring the same devoted room-sized audience.

events.title: Function 500 ft. Flux Aeterna
events.note: Local 500 and Public Works co-present. Techno in the main room; the loft usually has something quieter running alongside.

events.title: OhGeesy
events.note: Half of Shoreline Mafia, who are also on the Shoreline Amphitheatre bill tonight forty miles south — an odd bit of double-booking if you were planning to see both.

events.title: Próxima Parada
events.note: San Luis Obispo band playing warm, horn-lined soul-pop. A newer SF room that books more interestingly than its name suggests.

events.title: Black Swan + Perfect Blue double feature
events.note: Spoke Art presents. Aronofsky lifted more from Satoshi Kon than he has ever quite admitted, and seeing them back to back makes the case without anyone having to argue it. Perfect Blue alone screens at 8:50.

events.title: The Nexus Party
events.note: Part of SF/Bay Area Black Art Week. Twenty-five dollars for a party inside a contemporary art centre, which is a better use of the building than most of what happens in it.

events.title: Downtown First Thursdays
events.note: Free with RSVP. Two blocks of downtown closed off for bands, bars and vendors on the first Thursday of the month — the most reliable free thing in the financial district.

events.title: Free First Thursday
events.note: Free all afternoon on the first Thursday. A small Dogpatch museum that consistently punches above its square footage.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: The Thursday edition. Free music and food trucks between the library and City Hall.

events.title: Silent art auction preview: opening night
events.note: Free, RSVP requested. Hunters Point Shipyard holds one of the largest artist-studio communities in the country and opens up rarely — worth the trip out for that alone.

events.title: Terror Vault: Smashed Return to Hellville
events.note: Immersive haunt staged inside the 1874 Mint, running most nights through Halloween. The building is genuinely unnerving before anyone in makeup appears.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: A.C.T., mid-run.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: House default curtain time.

events.title: Jack Johnson with G. Love
events.note: Second and final night. Layers; it gets cold in that bowl after dark.

events.title: Fruit Bats
events.note: Sold out, doors 7. Eric D. Johnson has been writing gentle, unshowy songs for twenty-five years and has quietly become one of the more reliable live acts in this idiom. Matthew Logan Vasquez opens.

events.title: Maruja Limón
events.note: Barcelona quintet of women playing flamenco crossed with Latin and Mediterranean rhythm. A seated listening room, so the palmas carry.

events.title: Vincent Ingala
events.note: Multi-instrumentalist working the contemporary-jazz radio format. Competent and unsurprising; the room is the draw.

events.title: Combichrist
events.note: Norwegian aggrotech, which is industrial dance music for people who own boots. In a Shattuck beer hall, which is funnier than it should be.

events.title: Heavy Arts Ensemble
events.note: With Jelmars kumari and M. Sayyid — Sayyid is ex-Antipop Consortium, which puts real abstract-rap pedigree in a 150-cap room.

events.title: Bashfortheworld
events.note: Small Oakland room, sourced from the ticketing sweep; time unconfirmed.

events.title: Free First Thursday
events.note: Free galleries all day on the first Thursday. Maren Hassinger's Living Moving Growing is the one to see.

events.title: Italianamerican + American Boy
events.note: Scorsese's two seventies documentaries — his parents at their kitchen table, and Steven Prince talking too fast. The first is the best thing he ever shot.

events.title: The Cook
events.note: Thursday curtain is 8pm rather than 7.

events.title: $uicideboy$ with Shoreline Mafia
events.note: Shakewell, Drain and more underneath. Loud, nihilistic New Orleans rap at a 22,000-cap shed; $40 parking, and the bike path from Mountain View is genuinely the best way in.

events.title: Lynyrd Skynyrd
events.note: One original member and a very good covers band, at ninety-six dollars to start. The hillside and the sunset are doing a lot of the work.

events.title: Weedeater, Zeke, Royal Thunder, Yes Ma'am
events.note: North Carolina sludge, Seattle speed-punk and Atlanta heavy blues on one bill. Four bands, fifty-three dollars, and the best value in the South Bay this week if you can take the volume.

events.title: San Jose Sharks vs Florida Panthers — home opener
events.note: Opening night at the Tank, against the team that has won two of the last three Cups. Eighty-two dollars is not cheap, but a home opener has an atmosphere the other forty games do not.

events.title: Damitas Histeria (in Spanish)
events.note: Spanish-language stand-up at a chain club. Listed because the South Bay's Spanish-language comedy circuit is real and goes unrecorded elsewhere.

events.title: Geoff Tate: Operation: Mindcrime — The Final Chapter
events.note: Doors 7. Queensrÿche's original singer performing the 1988 concept album he is still best known for, billed as the last time. Prog-metal as period piece, done straight.

events.title: Ales & Tales stand-up
events.note: Free, tips appreciated. A brewery comedy night is not usually worth a line, but the Peninsula is thin enough this week that free and local counts.

events.title: MVFF49 opening night: Wild Horse Nine
events.venue: Christopher B. Smith Rafael Film Center
events.note: Martin McDonagh's new film, with John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell, opens the 49th Mill Valley Film Festival. Ninety-four features and eighty shorts from forty-five countries over eleven days across Mill Valley, San Rafael and Larkspur — this clears the drive on its own terms, and Peter Farrelly's I Play Rocky is the centrepiece later in the run.

events.title: Steel Pulse
events.note: Doors 8, ages 16+. Handsworth's finest, still the most politically serious of the British roots-reggae bands, and this is their only Bay date. A legacy act in a club, which is the specific case the drive test was written for.

events.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass, day one
events.note: Free, no ticket, seventy-one sets over six stages across three days. Friday's spine: Los Lobos at 4, My Morning Jacket at 4:55, Marty Stuart at 4:05, Molly Tuttle and Lukas Nelson closing at 7. Gates open 11 for a 1pm start. No bikes, scooters or Onewheels inside — leave them at the racks. Blankets under 6x8 only, no umbrellas, no hard coolers.

events.title: Robert Plant with Saving Grace and Suzi Dian
events.note: Doors 6:30, all ages, Rosie Flores guesting. Plant has spent six years on this band's version of Appalachian and British roots music, sharing the lead with Suzi Dian rather than fronting it. He also plays the park free on Sunday at 4:40 — this is the indoor, full-set version of the same idea.

events.title: Danny Elfman
events.note: First of two nights, and not the Tim Burton orchestral show — this is the rock set, Big Mess and Oingo Boingo material, with Robin Finck and Josh Freese from Nine Inch Nails and Nili Brosh on guitar. A homecoming for someone who started in a Los Angeles art-punk band.

events.title: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings
events.note: Two voices, two guitars, and the most exact harmony singing in American music. They played the Earle benefit last night and headline the park tomorrow afternoon; this is the one where you hear every word.

events.title: Madeon presents Victory Live
events.note: 18+. The French producer's full live rig rather than a DJ set. $45 at the Civic Center garage — BART or Muni to Civic Center and walk three minutes instead.

events.title: John Craigie
events.note: Portland songwriter who tells long jokes between short songs and has built a career on it. Anna Moss opens.

events.title: Lyrics Born
events.note: Tom Shimura has been rapping over live funk in this region since Latyrx in the mid-nineties, and his shows are closer to a soul revue than a rap gig. SundaY opens.

events.title: Deerhoof
events.note: Sold out, first of two nights. Thirty-two years of the most joyful difficult music in this city, in the 350-cap room that made them, in the year that room closes. Greyhound and Etch tonight; Las Sucias and Otioxi tomorrow. If you have never seen them, this is the last easy chance in the right venue.

events.title: Michelle Branch with SASAMI
events.note: Sold out, second of two nights.

events.title: Tyler Ballgame
events.note: 21+, with DUG. Basement room under Swedish American Hall, low ceiling, good for guitars.

events.title: The Bends
events.note: With Margot Sinclaire. All ages, twenty dollars, and the Rickshaw's sightlines are better than a room that shape has any right to.

events.title: Hamdi
events.note: With Flava D. UK bass and garage, first of two nights — the second adds Conducta and Sam Binga and is the stronger bill.

events.title: HEY, NOTHING
events.note: The Hound Tour. Atlanta duo making hushed, close-miked folk-pop. Venue publishes no times.

events.title: Bella Kay
events.note: With Hailey Picardi. A newer pop bill at the Independent, which books ahead of the curve often enough to be worth the risk.

events.title: Raynes
events.note: With David Wimbish & The Collection, whose orchestral-folk arrangements are the more interesting half of the bill.

events.title: SET with Mind Against, all night long
events.note: One duo, one room, all night — the format that separates a club night from a concert with a support act.

events.title: Quit Your Day Job presents: OUT OF OFFICE
events.note: Doors 9. A SoMa room that only recently became fetchable again after a domain change — worth watching now that its calendar is readable.

events.title: Algorithmic Art Assembly presents Kit Clayton
events.note: Clayton was making dub-techno out of code in the late nineties, before the vocabulary existed. Gray Area's Grand Theater is where the experimental emphasis in this digest has anywhere to look.

events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots
events.note: Penultimate performance. See Tuesday.

events.title: R-Evolution: one last celebration
events.note: Free, with DJs. Marco Cochrane's 55-foot sculpture leaves the Embarcadero after five years and the city is throwing it a send-off. Six hours on a plaza that is about to be rebuilt.

events.title: Block Fest: Tenderloin arts festival
events.note: Free with RSVP. Neighbourhood-organised arts programming in a district that gets policy attention and almost no cultural funding. The whole reason a digest like this exists.

events.title: Union Square Dances
events.note: Free outdoor social dancing on the square, lesson first. Three hours, no ticket, in the middle of downtown.

events.title: North Beach First Fridays art crawl
events.note: Free. Galleries and studios along Grant and the side streets stay open with wine on card tables. Walkable, and you can fold it into dinner.

events.title: Baukunst First Fridays: art, music and food
events.note: Free. The smaller, southern counterpart to the downtown art walks, and less crowded for it.

events.title: Fall Open Studios preview night
events.note: Free. Ninety-odd working studios in one Mission building, open for the evening before the weekend proper. Talking to the people who made the work is the point.

events.title: Battle of the Decades DJ party
events.note: Free with RSVP in a North Beach club. Free entry before eleven on a Friday in that neighbourhood is unusual enough to note.

events.title: Terror Vault: Smashed Return to Hellville
events.note: Running most nights to Halloween.

events.title: Movies at Mechanics' Presents
events.note: A 171-year-old members' library with a chess room and a film series. Free or cheap for members, small charge otherwise.

events.title: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: SF Neo-Futurists: thirty plays in sixty minutes, order decided by the audience shouting numbers, price set by a die roll at the door. The most reliably good cheap night in the city.

events.title: The Confessional
events.note: Long-form improv built from audience confessions. Endgames runs three shows a night on weekends and this is the strongest of them.

events.title: Golden Gate Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, 21+. The Function runs a free comedy night most days of the week; see the standing table rather than expecting each one listed separately.

events.title: Mission Street taco tour
events.note: Eighteen dollars for a guided crawl of Mission taquerias. You could do it yourself for less; the guide is the value if you don't know the ground.

events.title: Pay-what-you-can taco day
events.note: Free to $10, in Bayview. Genuinely pay-what-you-can rather than a marketing frame.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: A.C.T., mid-run.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: House default curtain time.

events.title: Raymix
events.note: The Mexican producer who made cumbia electrónica a chart format. Late start, dancing expected.

events.title: OFFAIAH
events.note: UK house DJ in a newer SoMa room. Time from the ticketing feed rather than the venue.

events.title: Inquisitive
events.note: Dogpatch warehouse with a $20 lot, which for a club night in this city counts as easy parking.

events.title: Madota
events.note: SoMa club, sourced from the ticketing sweep.

events.title: Playing the Dead
events.note: Grateful Dead covers in a North Beach pub, free. A tribute act by definition — included because the free-music circuit in this city runs on them, never because it is the best thing on.

events.title: Billy Strings
events.note: First of two nights. The most technically ferocious flatpicker of his generation, now filling arenas — which is the reason he is not in the park with everyone else this weekend. Listed for completeness; BART to Coliseum.

events.title: Snarky Puppy
events.note: Presented by SFJAZZ in an art deco palace rather than at their own hall. A large instrumental collective that treats groove as a compositional problem. All ages ticketed, no under-2s.

events.title: Death From Above 1979
events.note: Sold out, doors 7. Bass and drums, no guitar, still the loudest two-piece going. Rickshaw Billie's Burger Patrol open.

events.title: Hasan Minhaj and Ronny Chieng
events.note: Two shows tonight, at 7 and 9:30, and two more tomorrow. Two Daily Show alumni working very different registers — Minhaj narrative, Chieng deadpan. The early show is the better bet for a decent crowd.

events.title: The Curtis Family C-Notes
events.note: A family band out of Oakland playing funk, soul and gospel-inflected R&B, with the children doing most of the heavy lifting. Local, and better than the novelty framing suggests.

events.title: Luciano
events.note: Jamaican roots singer — the ticketing mirror lists him as Luciano (JM), which distinguishes him from the Swiss techno DJ of the same name. Worth confirming which before buying.

events.title: Jesse Barrera & Albert Posis
events.note: Doors 7. Two Filipino-American R&B songwriters who built their audiences on YouTube a decade before that was a normal route.

events.title: Oakland First Fridays
events.note: Free. Twenty blocks of Telegraph closed to traffic for art, food and stages. The largest recurring free street event in the East Bay, and it runs whatever else is on.

events.title: Oakland Art Murmur
events.note: Free. The gallery walk that First Fridays grew out of, and still the serious half of the evening. Garages off Broadway close their gates at 7 on weekdays — check before you park.

events.title: Friday Nights at OMCA with Shanté
events.note: Free, part of Nexus Black Art Week. Shanté plays the Garden Stage — smooth R&B with a gospel spine. The series runs April to October, so there are few of these left this year. BART to Lake Merritt, two minutes.

events.title: Gallery chat: Mildred Howard and Adrian Burrell
events.note: Free. Howard's five-decade retrospective is up in the galleries; hearing her in conversation with a younger Oakland artist is the better use of the hour.

events.title: Wet Sand
events.note: Elene Naveriani's film about a Black Sea village and the secret it has been keeping politely. Quiet and very hard.

events.title: The Cook
events.note: Mid-run.

events.title: Rock the Lodge: '90s hits and dance classics
events.note: Twenty dollars to dance in an Elks lodge, which is exactly the kind of municipal-hall programming this digest is meant to catch.

events.title: Oakland Critical Mass
events.note: Free, meet at the plaza. A mass ride rather than an organised event — no route published, which is the tradition.

events.title: Westbrae Pumpkin Patch
events.note: Free to browse, pumpkins $5–35. Opens for the season today in North Berkeley.

events.title: Pleasant Hill Night Market
events.note: Free. Pleasant Hill is not in the region lists — filed East Bay by proximity. A long way out from anywhere on this side of the bay.

events.title: Hayley Williams
events.note: With Magdalena Bay and Rico Nasty, which is a genuinely well-chosen support bill rather than filler. Paramore's singer solo, at twenty-five dollars to start — the best-value large show of the week.

events.title: Get The Led Out
events.note: A Led Zeppelin tribute, on the same night Robert Plant plays the Orpheum in person. Listed, never featured.

events.title: Ryan Castro
events.note: Medellín reggaetón with a street-corner origin story he still leans on. A hundred and twenty dollars to start, which is the price of a Colombian act with no Bay history.

events.title: Sploinky Rave
events.note: A rave in a metal club, which produces a better crowd than either scene manages alone.

events.title: Third Party
events.note: UK big-room house duo. Street parking is free after 6 and Caltrain Sunnyvale is a six-minute walk, which makes this the easiest late night in the South Bay.

events.title: South First Fridays art walk
events.note: Free. Galleries, museums and studios along South First open late, with street programming between them. The best free evening in the home region this week.

events.title: Ginny Hogan
events.note: Two nights. A writer-comic with a sharp tech-adjacent act, which plays differently in Sunnyvale than anywhere else.

events.title: Murray Hidary
events.note: MindTravel-style improvised piano heard through headphones while walking a park at dusk. Filed under oddities; the format is real but the listing carried no confirmed time.

events.title: Everywhen in the Woods
events.venue: Santa Cruz Mountains, near Los Gatos
events.note: A three-day camping festival in the redwoods with music, workshops and communal meals, listed as starting today. Neither the dates nor the lineup could be confirmed from a primary source this week — treat as unverified before you pack a tent.

events.title: John Oates & The Good Road Band
events.note: Doors 7. Not the Hall & Oates show — Oates has spent the last decade playing acoustic blues and Americana with a real band, and it is the more interesting half of his career.

events.title: Opening: Live The Moment Light
events.note: Free. The Art Center's openings are the Peninsula's only regular gallery evenings, and it is a fifteen-minute walk from Caltrain Palo Alto.

events.title: Free First Friday
events.note: Free all day, in the old county courthouse on the square. The building's stained-glass dome is worth the visit by itself.

events.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass, day two
events.note: Free, gates 9am. The deepest of the three days: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings at 3:50, Rilo Kiley at 4:55 stepping in for Alison Krauss, Old Crow Medicine Show and Steve Earle & the Hardly Strictly Dukes both closing at 7, with Hot Tuna Acoustic and Alison Brown earlier. Six stages, 750,000 people over the weekend, and the west end of the park effectively closed to cars.

events.title: Hiromi & Kazunori Kumagai
events.note: Sold out. The programme changed from the Trio Project to a duo with tap dancer Kazunori Kumagai, which is the better accident — Hiromi's playing is percussive enough that a tap dancer is a peer rather than an accompanist. She returns tomorrow with the trio. Not featured only because both nights are gone.

events.title: My Morning Jacket
events.note: First of two nights in a 1,315-cap room, on a weekend they also play the park for free. Jim James's reverb is built for that ceiling.

events.title: Danny Elfman
events.note: Second night. See Friday.

events.title: Renée Fleming Sings Strauss
events.note: The evening performance of the Strauss programme, and the one to pick if you want the hall full.

events.title: Igorrr
events.note: Sold out. Gautier Serre welds baroque harpsichord to breakcore and death metal, and it should not work. Secret Chiefs 3 and Violent Magic Orchestra open — one of the strangest and best-sequenced bills of the year.

events.title: Geordie Greep
events.note: An evening with. Black Midi's former singer solo, doing lounge-jazz-as-horror with a large band and an unreliable narrator. Tickets still available, which will not last.

events.title: Deerhoof
events.note: Sold out, second night. Las Sucias and Otioxi open — Las Sucias make abrasive reggaeton-industrial in Spanish and are the better argument for tonight over last night.

events.title: Ecca Vandal
events.note: With Speed of Light. Melbourne singer who moves between hardcore and rap without either sounding like a costume. Two nights.

events.title: Hamdi
events.note: Second night, with Conducta and Sam Binga. The deeper bill of the two.

events.title: ROYA
events.note: With 1ycia.

events.title: Kreayshawn
events.note: The Oakland rapper whose 2011 single was inescapable and whose career afterwards was a case study in what a viral hit costs. The venue's calendar pages were 503ing all week, so this is from the ticketing feed.

events.title: JANTSEN
events.note: VEXRA and Public Works co-present. Heavy bass, late.

events.title: SUB DISTRICT: Calcium
events.note: Doors 9.

events.title: Elephante
events.note: With RayRay, AMIDY and Nikademis. DJ_DAVE plays the smaller room the same night.

events.title: Shingo Nakamura
events.note: Melodic progressive house inside an 1874 granite vault. The building is the reason to go.

events.title: Glyders
events.note: Chicago duo playing loose, vintage-toned guitar music in a tiny Lower Haight bar.

events.title: New exhibitions open: RM's collection and Raven Chacon
events.note: Opens today and runs to February. Korean works from RM's personal collection, many never shown in the US, alongside a new Raven Chacon commission about Navajo Nation land. The Chacon is the one that will still matter in five years.

events.title: Free museum day for Bay Area residents
events.note: Free for Bay Area residents on the first Saturday. The catch this week is geography: the de Young sits inside the festival footprint, so walk in from the east or come early.

events.title: Free museum day for Bay Area residents
events.note: Free for Bay Area residents, and far enough west of the festival to be reachable. The Rodin holdings and the view over the Golden Gate come free with it.

events.title: African Arts Festival
events.note: Free, part of the Yerba Buena Gardens Festival. Music, dance and makers on the lawn downtown — and the best option this weekend if the park crowd is more than you want.

events.title: Bay Area Maya Festival
events.note: Fifth year, free. Organised by and for the Bay's Maya community — Yucatec and Mam language, music and food, on a community college campus in the Mission.

events.title: Fall Open Studios
events.note: Free, the main weekend day. Ninety studios; go for the third floor.

events.title: Pop-Ups on the Plaza: Latine makers
events.note: Free. Latine makers alongside the Saturday market, which is the busiest and best of the week.

events.title: A New Leaf
events.note: Fifteen dollars including themed snacks and gallery admission, which makes Elaine May's 1971 debut the cheapest full afternoon in the city. It is also very funny.

events.title: Gray Area x TIAT: Processing Community Day
events.note: A day of workshops and talks around Processing, the open-source language that put a generation of artists into code.

events.title: BATS Improv
events.note: Long-form improv at Fort Mason, running most Saturdays through the year. Reliable rather than surprising, and the bay is right outside.

events.title: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Thirty plays in sixty minutes. See Friday.

events.title: Drunk Theatre: Nightmare on Valencia St.
events.note: A Halloween special of an improv format that is exactly what the name says. Valencia between 17th and 20th has effectively no parking — BART to 16th and walk.

events.title: The Confessional
events.note: See Friday. Your Fucked Up Relationship follows at 9.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: Matinee, with an evening performance at 8. A.C.T.'s season opener, running to 18 October.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Evening performance; the Playhouse usually also runs a Saturday matinee but does not publish per-date times.

events.title: Billy Strings
events.note: Second night; a two-day ticket exists and cannot be split. Listed for completeness.

events.title: Jon Batiste
events.note: An outdoor amphitheatre in October, which means cold by nine and worth it. Batiste's live show swings between New Orleans piano tradition and stadium gospel-pop, sometimes in the same song.

events.title: Hasan Minhaj and Ronny Chieng
events.note: Two shows, 6 and 9. The late one will be the looser of the four across the weekend.

events.title: Miles Electric Band featuring Keyon Harrold
events.note: Two nights. Davis alumni playing the Bitches Brew and On the Corner material with Harrold, who has the hardest job in music, on trumpet. Loud, electric, and not a tribute in the polite sense.

events.title: Castle Rat
events.note: Sold out, doors 6:30. Brooklyn doom with full costume and narrative, supported by Unto Others and Wraith Knight. Committed to the bit in the best way.

events.title: Handsome Dick Manitoba
events.note: The Dictators' frontman in a 150-cap Telegraph room, with The Bonstones and Fuzz Attack. First-wave New York punk at arm's length.

events.title: 52nd Oakland Black Cowboy Parade & Festival
events.note: Free. Parade steps off at 10 and the festival runs to 6 — horses, line dancing, pony rides and food in West Oakland. Fifty-two years of the Oakland Black Cowboy Association keeping the history of Black cowboys in the West visible, and there is nothing else like it in the region.

events.title: Oaktoberfest in the Dimond
events.note: Free entry, two days, five stages. Nineteenth year at Fruitvale and MacArthur, with 200-plus beers behind the drink packages. The German bands are real German bands.

events.title: Bay Area Anarchist Book Fair
events.note: Free, 28th year. Small presses, zines and a talks programme in a hall on Telegraph. Genuinely the best small-press browsing of the year in this region.

events.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part 2 — Exile
events.note: Screening in partnership with the Mill Valley Film Festival. Julia Loktev's documentary on independent Russian journalists and what happened to them. Long, and the only way to see it.

events.title: The Cook
events.note: Matinee at 2, evening at 7:30. Closes 11 October.

events.title: Bon Marché 2nd Hand Market
events.note: Secondhand clothes and objects in a gallery rather than a car park, which raises the quality of both the stock and the browsing.

events.title: Tabletop Library grand opening
events.note: Free. A lending library for board games opening in Berkeley, which is either a very good idea or a very Berkeley one, and probably both.

events.title: Science in the Park
events.note: Free. Hayward is not in the region lists — filed East Bay by proximity. Hands-on science aimed at families, on a campus with a long view over the bay.

events.title: Kehlani
events.note: First of two nights, with Durand Bernarr, Isaia Huron and more. An Oakland singer selling out a 22,000-cap shed forty miles from home; the R&B songwriting has got sharper, not softer, with the scale.

events.title: All Shall Perish, Carnifex, Extermination Dismemberment, Mauled
events.note: Four bands from 6pm. All Shall Perish formed in Oakland and this is closer to a hometown show than the billing suggests.

events.title: Sonic Live In Concert
events.note: Game music played live to picture. A format that has become a genre of its own; bring someone under twelve or don't bother.

events.title: San Jose Sharks vs Los Angeles Kings
events.note: Opening weekend, and a divisional rival. VTA Race Street is an eight-minute walk and saves you the $15 lot.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs San Diego Gulls
events.note: AHL hockey at three in the afternoon for twenty-three dollars — minor league, walkable, and exactly the kind of cheap local sport this digest is for. They play again tomorrow from $13.

events.title: Markus Schulz
events.note: Long-form trance from a DJ who has been playing six-hour sets since before that was a marketing angle.

events.title: Ginny Hogan
events.note: Second night.

events.title: Nature scavenger hunt: count birds, bugs and species
events.note: Free with RSVP, at the restored 1941 boathouse on the Palo Alto baylands. A bioblitz dressed up as a scavenger hunt, which is the right way round.

events.title: Teen boating program
events.note: Free. Small-boat sailing for teenagers on the Redwood City waterfront — municipal programming that never reaches a listings site.

events.title: Santa Cruz Porchfest
events.note: Free, all ages, first year: fifty-plus sets on fourteen porches and stoops across downtown, with an after-party at Abbott Square from 6:30. A borderline call against the outer-region bar — nothing would make it a top-three event in a Hardly Strictly week — but it is free, unrepeatable as a first edition, and the drive over the hill is 45 minutes if you go before three.

events.title: MVFF49
events.venue: Christopher B. Smith Rafael Film Center
events.note: The festival's first full weekend, across Rafael, the Sequoia in Mill Valley and the Lark in Larkspur. Ninety-four features, and the programme is 61 per cent work by women and nonbinary directors. Bridge toll is southbound only, so the drive over is free.

events.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass, day three
events.note: Free, gates 9am, and the strongest closing day: Robert Plant with Saving Grace at 4:40, Punch Brothers at 3:50, The Record Company at 3:45, Emmylou Harris closing at 5:45. Plant plays the Orpheum on Friday for money and the park on Sunday for nothing, which tells you something about the festival.

events.title: 52nd Castro Street Fair
events.note: Free with a $10–20 suggested donation, this year themed 'Where We Belong'. Harvey Milk started it in 1974 to show that gay-owned businesses were a neighbourhood economy; since 1998 it has given $1.6m back to community groups. Stages, DJs and hundreds of makers. It overlaps the festival almost exactly — Muni Castro puts you at the gate, and the Castro Art Mart at Market and Noe runs alongside it.

events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots — final performance
events.note: Closing matinee, with a post-performance talkback hosted by music director Eun Sun Kim with conductor Clelia Cafiero. The last chance to see a 98-year-old composer's own libretto staged by the company that premiered it in America.

events.title: Renée Fleming Sings Strauss
events.note: Final performance of the Strauss programme, Sunday matinee. Santtu-Matias Rouvali conducting.

events.title: Lang Lang
events.note: A recital on the same day as the Symphony's Strauss matinee, which means the hall turns over between them. Listings agree on the date and not on the time — confirm the curtain before you build an evening around it.

events.title: Hiromi: The Trio Project
events.note: Sold out. The trio with Simon Phillips and James Genus, the night after the tap duo. Two entirely different shows from the same pianist in two days.

events.title: My Morning Jacket
events.note: Second night.

events.title: Bilmuri
events.note: With Knuckle Puck and NOVELISTS. Johnny Franck's project has gone from metalcore in-joke to a genuinely large touring act on the strength of writing actual hooks.

events.title: Groundation
events.note: Sonoma County roots reggae with real jazz harmony underneath — a Bay Area band with more standing in Europe than at home. The Quasi Kings open.

events.title: Acid Mothers Temple featuring Cotton Casino
events.note: Tickets still available, which is the surprise of the week. Kawabata Makoto's Japanese psychedelic collective with Cotton Casino back on synth and vocals — thirty years of the loudest, longest cosmic guitar music going. Magick Potion and The Green Door open, DJ after.

events.title: Rum Jungle
events.note: Australian four-piece with a loose, sun-bleached guitar sound. Trestles open.

events.title: Keznamdi
events.note: 21+. Jamaican singer working a modern roots-and-dancehall hybrid, from a family deep in the music.

events.title: rusowsky
events.note: Sold out. Madrid producer-singer at the centre of a Spanish alt-pop scene that has moved very fast in two years.

events.title: Ecca Vandal
events.note: Second night, with Speed of Light.

events.title: RC AVENUE
events.note: With Ebony Loren.

events.title: Octo Octa: Castro Street Fair after party
events.note: Polyglamorous presents, doors 5:30 for a 6pm start — early, because it catches the fair as it closes. Maya Bouldry-Morrison plays warm, rave-literate house; BEYA and Mark O'Brien alongside.

events.title: Litquake Out Loud + Book Fair
events.note: Free. Readings and a book fair on the Esplanade — the free outdoor curtain-raiser to Litquake proper, which runs 8–24 October. Small presses in the sun, which beats a bookshop reading.

events.title: San Francisco Fleet Week opens
events.note: Free. Fleet Week runs 4–12 October, and today is the quiet opening — band performances start Monday, ship tours at Piers 27 and 35 on the 7th and 8th, and the Blue Angels air show is the 9th to the 11th, not this weekend. Come back next week for the flying.

events.title: Lindy in the Park
events.note: Free swing dancing on JFK Drive every Sunday, thirty-odd years running. It sits inside the festival footprint this weekend, so expect a much larger audience than usual and check that JFK is open at that end.

events.title: Sunday Roller Disco
events.note: Free. The park's roller disco has been running on Sundays since the seventies and is the single most reliably joyful free thing in this city. Also inside the festival footprint today.

events.title: Castro Art Mart mini block party
events.note: Free. Local makers a block up from the street fair, and a quieter place to actually look at things.

events.title: Free first Sunday
events.note: Free for everyone on the first Sunday of the month. The Ha Chong-Hyun retrospective is the reason to use it.

events.title: Fall Open Studios
events.note: Free, final day.

events.title: Pickwick Vintage Show
events.note: Curated vintage clothing and jewellery, with an entry charge. Dealer-quality stock and priced accordingly.

events.title: HEAD WEST Marketplace
events.note: Free. The rotating maker market lands at the Ferry Building this weekend — its location changes most months, so this one is worth noting when it is central.

events.title: Fort Mason Farmers Market
events.note: Free, Sundays. Smaller and calmer than the Ferry Plaza, with the bay at the end of the row.

events.title: Indie film screenings + tech talk on filmmaking
events.note: Shorts plus a craft conversation. The kind of afternoon where the Q&A is better than the programme.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: Sunday matinee. Runs to 18 October.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Sunday matinee; curtain time is the house default.

events.title: The Green
events.note: Sold out, doors 7. Honolulu's most successful island-reggae band, with Johnny Suite. Sold out weeks ago, which says more about the Bay's Pacific Islander audience than any chart does.

events.title: Miles Electric Band featuring Keyon Harrold
events.note: Second night.

events.title: Shearling
events.note: A Sunday show in a 150-cap room, which is the format this club is best at.

events.title: In Her Own Words x Every Avenue
events.note: Doors 6:30. Emo revival and a 2000s Michigan pop-punk band on a co-headline, which is a very specific and well-served nostalgia.

events.title: Oaktoberfest in the Dimond, day two
events.note: Free entry, second and quieter day, 10 to 5. Better if you actually want to talk to anyone.

events.title: OMCA Architecture Walk and Talk
events.note: Free, with Council on Architecture members. Kevin Roche's 1969 terraced building is one of the best pieces of architecture in the city and is usually discussed only as a container for the collection.

events.title: Band of Outsiders
events.note: Godard's 1964 film, in the series built around the Gvido Augusts poster designs. The Louvre run and the Madison are the reason it is still quoted.

events.title: La Gradiva
events.note: Screening with the Mill Valley Film Festival, which is how the East Bay gets a piece of a Marin festival.

events.title: The Cook
events.note: Matinee at 2, evening at 7. Closes 11 October.

events.title: Kehlani
events.note: Second night, and cheaper than Saturday's. The bike path from Mountain View remains the only sane way in.

events.title: Hammerfall, Evergrey, Elvenking
events.note: Three bands of Swedish and Italian power metal, played entirely straight. Forty-seven dollars for a genre that lives on exactly this kind of bill.

events.title: Little Italy San Jose Italian Festival
events.note: Free or donation. Eight hours of food, music and bocce in the North San Pedro blocks. The closest thing the home region has to a street fair this week, and free.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs San Diego Gulls
events.note: Thirteen dollars for professional hockey on a Sunday afternoon. The cheapest live ticket in this digest.

events.title: Gaurav Kapoor
events.note: Hindi-language stand-up in a 3,000-seat hall, which is a fair measure of how large the South Bay's South Asian comedy audience now is.

events.title: Ricardo Quevedo (in Spanish)
events.note: Colombian stand-up, matinee.

events.title: Chad Opitz
events.note: Standing Sunday booking at the Sunnyvale club.

events.title: Hardly Strictly Out of the Park: Kathleen Edwards
events.note: Doors 7, with Fantastic Cat. An official Hardly Strictly offshoot forty miles down the Peninsula — Edwards came out of a long silence a few years ago writing better than before, and this is the only way to see a festival artist seated and indoors. The best thing on the Peninsula this week.

events.title: MVFF49
events.venue: Christopher B. Smith Rafael Film Center
events.note: Second Sunday of the festival's first weekend. Jesse Eisenberg closes the run with The Debut on the 11th, so this weekend is the part you can still get into.
